newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX closes at new record high, volume light.
newsitem.headline: German DAX closes at new record high, volume light.

text.p: German shares closed slightly higher on Friday at another record high, but trade was thin following Thursday's national holiday and ahead of U.S. jobs data due out at 1230 GMT, traders said.
The DAX index of 30 blue chip shares closed floor trade up 6.78 points, or 0.25 percent, at 2,683.28, overtaking a high of 2680.10 touched during Wednesday's close.
Dealers said the stocks were supported by the dollar's strength against the mark which aids export-oriented German shares.
Following the Germany Unity Day holiday on Thursday many people had taken a long weekend. "Most people closed their books for the week on Wednesday," said one trader.
Volume was also limited ahead of the release of U.S. jobless figures. "Traders aren't going to want to stick their neck out ahead of the unemployment figures," said one dealer.

Traders said players on the sidelines could come back into the market later in the day when the DAX is traded electronically and the index could then test the psychological and technical level of 2,700 points.

Building group Holzmann AG was the loss leader, tumbling 18 marks, over five percent, to 332 marks, after a Bild newspaper report said that its chief executive could be sacked and replaced by the head of diversified industrial group Metallgesellschaft AG.
MG denied the report as nonsense and Holzmann called the article "factually incorrect and speculative." Holzmann on Wednesday denied reports that the group had liquidity problems.
Airline company Lufthansa gained ground, with traders saying the firm was cutting three South American routes due to lack of demand.
